summary: Per-vehicle 3D collision contact computation. Transforms the queried contact point into vehicle-local space, performs an AABB overlap test against the vehicle bounds, iterates the packed collision-geometry list to find the closest penetrating vertex, computes contact normal and penetration depth, and writes the assembled contact response into an outgoing collision buffer.

Query the contact point via sub_4EA930(&v64) and take its x/y/z components.
Transform the contact point into vehicle-local coordinates using the orientation matrix this[3372..3380] (this+0x34B0..0x34D0).
Build the AABB test volume by combining this[459..461] (this+0x72C..0x734) with this[465..470] (this+0x744..0x758) plus the half-extent at a2+24.
AABB overlap test: reject the contact when the local contact point falls outside the box on any of the three axes.
Obtain the packed collision-geometry list handle via LinkedListIndexedAccessor_c230(0) and read its total size with PackedArrayTotalSize.
Iterate every packed geometry vertex, fetching each entry with PackedArrayIndexLookup.
Transform each vertex into vehicle-local space, test it inside the AABB, and track the closest vertex by minimum squared distance.
Compute penetration depth from this+0x3B70 minus the closest distance, clamp at zero, and derive the contact normal from the closest vertex position.
Acquire the outgoing collision buffer via ArithmeticComparison_a010 and store the contact state (negative marker, request pointer, state word) into it.
Write the contact normal and direction into the buffer, rotating through the orientation matrix this+0x34B4..0x34DC, and normalize the resulting vector.
Run VehicleGeometryProximityTest on the assembled contact point/normal in the buffer.
Run VehicleProjectedPosition to apply the projected-contact correction to the contact data.
Compute the final contact response: clamp the normal component, apply the 0.2 restitution factor to the impulse, and normalize the resulting direction into the buffer.
